items.title: Section: The Five Purifying Objects Formally Named; Five Skilful Objects Open

items.zh: 是名第五多尋思行補特伽羅淨行所緣。如是總名淨行所緣。云何名為善巧所緣？謂此所緣略有五種。一、蘊善巧，二、界善巧，三、處善巧，四、緣起善巧，五、處非處善巧。
items.en: This is the fifth: the purifying object for practitioners dominated by discursive thought. Altogether, these are called the purifying objects. What are skilful objects? Briefly, this object is of five kinds: skillfulness regarding the aggregates, skillfulness regarding the elements, skillfulness regarding the sense-fields, skillfulness regarding dependent origination, and skillfulness regarding what is possible and impossible.

items.zh: 蘊善巧者，云何蘊？云何蘊善巧？謂蘊有五。則色蘊、受蘊、想蘊、行蘊、識蘊。

items.title: The Five Aggregates Defined; Aggregate-Skillfulness Opens

items.zh: 云何色蘊？謂諸所有色，一切皆是四大種及四大種所造。此復若過去、若未來、若現在、若內、若外、若麁、若細、若劣、若勝、若遠、若近。總名色蘊。云何受蘊？謂或順樂觸為緣諸受，或順苦觸為緣諸受，或順不苦不樂觸為緣諸受。復有六受身。則眼觸所生受，耳、鼻、舌、身、意觸所生受。總名受蘊。云何想蘊？謂有相想、無相想、狹小想、廣大想、無量想、無諸所有無所有處想。復有六想身。則眼觸所生想，耳、鼻、舌、身、意觸所生想。總名想蘊。云何行蘊？謂六思身。則眼觸所生思，耳、鼻、舌、身、意觸所生思。復有所餘，除受及想諸心法等。總名行蘊。云何識蘊？謂心、意、識。復有六識身。則眼識，耳、鼻、舌、身、意識。總名識蘊。前受、想、行蘊及此識蘊，皆有過去、未來、現在、內、外等差別，如前廣說。是名為蘊。云何蘊善巧？謂善了知如所說蘊種種差別性、非一眾多性，除此法外，更無所得、無所分別，是名略說蘊善巧義。
items.en: What is the aggregate of form? Whatever form there is, all of it is either the four great elements or what is derived from them. What is the aggregate of feeling? It is feeling conditioned by a contact tending towards pleasure, or towards suffering, or towards neither — together with the six bodies of feeling arising from the six sense-contacts. What is the aggregate of perception? It is perception with characteristic, without characteristic, narrow, vast, immeasurable, and the perception of nothing-whatsoever — together with the six bodies of perception. What is the aggregate of formations? It is the six bodies of volition, together with all other mental factors apart from feeling and perception. What is the aggregate of consciousness? It is mind, mentation, and consciousness, together with the six bodies of consciousness. What is skillfulness regarding the aggregates? It is thoroughly knowing that the aggregates, as described, each differ from one another and are each not single but manifold — and that apart from these phenomena, nothing further is to be found or discriminated. This, briefly, is the meaning of skillfulness regarding the aggregates.

items.zh: 云何名蘊種種差別性？謂色蘊異、受蘊異，乃至識蘊異，是名種種差別性。云何名蘊非一眾多性？謂色蘊非一眾多品類。大種所造差別故，去來今等品類差別故。是名色蘊非一眾多性。如是餘蘊，隨其所應皆當了知。云何除此法外，更無所得、無所分別？謂唯蘊可得、唯事可得。非離蘊外有我可得，有常恒住無變易法是可得者。亦無少法是我所有。故除此外，更無所得、無所分別。

items.title: Element-Skillfulness: Eighteen Elements as Eighteen Seeds

items.zh: 云何界？云何界善巧？謂界有十八。則眼界、色界、眼識界，耳界、聲界、耳識界，鼻界、香界、鼻識界，舌界、味界、舌識界，身界、觸界、身識界，意界、法界、意識界。是名為界。若復於彼十八種法，從別別界、別別種子、別別種姓生起出現，如實了知、忍可、審察，名界善巧。如實了知十八種法，從別別界別別而轉，即於因緣而得善巧，是故說此名界善巧。
items.en: What are the elements? What is skillfulness regarding the elements? The elements are eighteen: the eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element; the ear, sound, and ear-consciousness elements; the nose, smell, and nose-consciousness elements; the tongue, taste, and tongue-consciousness elements; the body, touch, and body-consciousness elements; and the mind, phenomena, and mind-consciousness elements. This is called the elements. Truly knowing, assenting to, and closely examining that these eighteen phenomena each arise from their own distinct element, their own distinct seed, their own distinct nature — this is called skillfulness regarding the elements.

items.title: Sense-Field-Skillfulness: Twelve Fields and the Three Conditions

items.zh: 云何處？云何處善巧？謂處有十二。則眼處、色處、耳處、聲處、鼻處、香處、舌處、味處、身處、觸處、意處、法處。是名為處。處善巧者，謂眼為增上緣，色為所緣緣，等無間滅意為等無間緣，生起眼識，及相應法。耳為增上緣，聲為所緣緣，等無間滅意為等無間緣，生起耳識及相應法。如是乃至意為等無間緣，此生作意為增上緣，法為所緣緣，生起意識及相應法。如是六識身及相應法，皆由三緣而得流轉。謂增上緣、所緣緣、等無間緣。若於如是諸內外處緣得善巧，名處善巧。
items.en: What are the sense-fields? What is skillfulness regarding them? The sense-fields are twelve: the eye and form fields, the ear and sound fields, the nose and smell fields, the tongue and taste fields, the body and touch fields, and the mind and phenomena fields. This is called the sense-fields. Skillfulness regarding the sense-fields is: the eye serves as the dominant condition, form as the object condition, and the immediately-preceding cessation of mind as the immediate condition, giving rise to eye-consciousness and its associated factors — and likewise for the ear and the rest, up to the mind: the immediately-preceding cessation of mind as the immediate condition, the attention arising from it as the dominant condition, and mental objects as the object condition, giving rise to mind-consciousness and its associated factors; all six consciousnesses and their associated factors arise through these three conditions: the dominant condition, the object condition, and the immediate condition. Attaining skillfulness regarding these three conditions across all the internal and external sense-fields is called skillfulness regarding the sense-fields.

blocks.text: The second category of object: **skilful objects** (善巧所緣), five kinds of understanding that clear confusion about what we are made of. One passage (0433c23) is untranslated.
Skill regarding the aggregates, the elements, the sense-fields, dependent origination, and what is possible and impossible. Venerable Miào Jìng: skill in the sense-fields includes the faculties.

Form is "the four great elements or what derives from them"; feeling, conditioned by contact; perception, recognising; formations, intention and the rest; consciousness, "mind, mentation, and consciousness".

The untranslated prose (0433c23) gives three points of skill: the aggregates are **different from one another**; each is **not single but manifold** (form by elements and derivatives, by past, present, and future); and **apart from them nothing else is found**: "only aggregates, only events; no self apart from the aggregates, nothing permanent, nothing that belongs to a self."

Eighteen: the six faculties, six objects, six consciousnesses. Skill means "truly knowing that these eighteen phenomena each arise from their own distinct element", their own seed. Venerable Miào Jìng: element here means causal condition.

Twelve: six faculties and six objects. Skill means knowing how consciousness arises: "the eye serves as the dominant condition, form as the object condition, and the immediately preceding mind as the immediately preceding condition." Venerable Miào Jìng: the Lesser Vehicle does not speak of manas, so attention is named the dominant condition.

These are the "maps" of Buddhist psychology met on Days 3–4 and in the Hundred Dharmas. Here they are not theory but objects of meditation: each map, practised, cures a particular confusion about the self.

quiz.q: What are the five skilful objects, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say "skilful" means?
options: the aggregates, elements, sense-fields, dependent origination, possible and impossible; skillfulness is penetrating wisdom
quiz.why: "Skillfulness regarding the aggregates, the elements, the sense-fields, dependent origination, and what is possible and impossible." Venerable Miào Jìng: these five skills — "skilful" means penetrating wisdom.

quiz.q: The note says "faculty-skill" is a sixth, not included here. What do the masters say?
options: Miào Jìng: sense-field skill already includes the six faculties; Cháng Bǎi: not in the Hearers' Ground, but fascicle 57 details twenty-two faculties
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: sense-field skill includes the six faculties, so faculty-skill is within it. Master Cháng Bǎi: there is also faculty-skill, not covered in the Hearers' Ground, but explained in detail — twenty-two faculties — in fascicle 57.

quiz.q: The consciousness aggregate is mind, mentation, and consciousness. How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the three words?
options: mind means gathering, mentation means support or deliberation, consciousness means discerning
quiz.why: "What is the aggregate of consciousness? It is mind, mentation, and consciousness." Venerable Miào Jìng: mind means gathering; mentation can mean support or deliberation; consciousness means discerning.

quiz.q: What is skillfulness regarding the elements, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng say element, seed, and nature mean?
options: knowing eighteen names; three different meanings
truly knowing that the eighteen arise from their own element, seed, and nature; three names, one meaning — seed
quiz.why: "Truly knowing, assenting to, and closely examining that these eighteen phenomena each arise from their own distinct element, their own distinct seed, their own distinct nature — this is called skillfulness regarding the elements." Venerable Miào Jìng: element, seed, and nature are different words with the same meaning — seed.

quiz.q: Which of the four conditions does skill in the elements especially penetrate, according to the masters?
options: both agree: the causal condition — the elements show all phenomena arise from seeds
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the eighteen elements here refer to the causal condition; penetrating the causal condition is "skillfulness." Master Cháng Bǎi: the meaning of "element" here is that all phenomena are produced from seeds; among the four conditions, one penetrates the causal condition.

quiz.q: In sense-field skill, what three conditions produce eye-consciousness, and why, according to Venerable Miào Jìng, is the causal condition not mentioned?
options: eye as dominant, form as object, the just-ceased mind as immediate condition; the causal condition was covered under the elements
quiz.why: "The eye serves as the dominant condition, form as the object condition, and the immediately-preceding cessation of mind as the immediate condition, giving rise to eye-consciousness and its associated factors." Venerable Miào Jìng: these are three conditions; the causal condition is not mentioned because it was covered under the eighteen elements.

quiz.q: The English says the remaining consciousnesses arise "likewise," but for mind-consciousness the text names attention as the dominant condition. How do the masters explain this?
options: Miào Jìng: the Lesser Vehicle does not teach manas, so attention is named; Cháng Bǎi: this is for hearers, who do not teach manas
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the Lesser Vehicle does not speak of manas, so the mental factor of attention is called the dominant condition. Master Cháng Bǎi: because this teaching is shared with the hearer vehicle, which speaks of neither eight consciousnesses nor manas. The English "likewise" flattens this special case.
